Every other planet in this chart is doing perfectly fine — comfortably neutral, nothing broken, nothing dramatic. Just one placement running at full power: the one in charge of staying calm and doing the arithmetic while the rest of the stadium loses its mind.

That's a real, computed match for a reputation built on finishing a World Cup final with a six and making bowling changes nobody in the commentary box saw coming.

2004–05 · THE ARRIVAL
FILE PHOTO · MAR 2008

A small-town wicketkeeper nobody had a scouting report for.

148 off 123 vs Pakistan, the breakout innings
  • ODI debut 23 December 2004 against Bangladesh — a duck, first ball. Four months later in Visakhapatnam he made 148 against Pakistan: long hair, a helicopter shot the commentators didn't have a name for yet.
  • Two years out of a government job in Kharagpur, batting at No. 3 for India.
🔭 The opening years of a single Rahu mahadasha that would go on to run his entire international career, debut to retirement, without handing over once.

2007–2011 · THE CAPTAIN
FILE PHOTO · OCT 2007

Handed the keys to a dressing room of seniors he used to watch on TV.

2 World Cups as captain, four years apart
  • Made captain for the inaugural T20 World Cup in 2007 — a format nobody had played before, won by a side missing several senior players. Delhi gave the team a felicitation with the Prime Minister days later.
  • 2 April 2011: the ODI World Cup final, an unbeaten 91, and the six that ended a 28-year wait. He'd promoted himself up the order that night, ahead of a red-hot Yuvraj Singh.
🔭 Still inside the same Rahu stretch. Rahu's classic reading is audacity — promoting yourself to bat first on the biggest night of your career is a fairly literal example of that.

Run out WC 2019 semi-final, his last international innings
  • 30 December 2014: resigned the Test captaincy overnight, mid-series in Australia, handing over to Virat Kohli without a press conference.

🔭 The closing years of that same 18-year Rahu mahadasha, which hands over in May 2022. Rahu rarely does a farewell lap — it tends to just stop, and you find out afterwards that was the finish line.

The messy bits

Everything you're actually here for

Sixteen years at the top means a few real storms. All of the below is public record — where he wasn't personally implicated, that travels with the claim in the same breath.

⚖️ The scandal that landed on his team, not him
What's public

The 2013 IPL betting and spot-fixing case named Gurunath Meiyappan — a Chennai Super Kings team official and son-in-law of then-BCCI president N. Srinivasan — as having passed on team information. A Supreme Court-appointed panel found him guilty; CSK (and Rajasthan Royals) were suspended from the IPL for the 2016 and 2017 seasons.

Dhoni was CSK's captain throughout. He was never named or charged in the case itself. He played the two suspension years for Rising Pune Supergiant, then returned to a reinstated CSK in 2018 — and won the title that same season, his third with the franchise.

What the chart hints

The whole episode sits inside his long Rahu mahadasha. Rahu's classic reading is reputational heat by association — close enough to the fire to feel it, without ever being named in it.

It's also worth noting: the comeback title arrived the moment the ban lifted, still inside that same period.

🏏 The run-out that ended an era
What's public

10 July 2019, World Cup semi-final vs New Zealand at Old Trafford. Chasing 240, he was run out going for a second run with the equation still alive; India lost by 18 runs. No one knew it at the time, but it was his final international innings.

No retirement followed for over a year. He simply stopped being picked for Tests and T20Is, and wasn't part of the ODI XI again either.

What the chart hints

The dying stretch of the same Rahu mahadasha that started his career in 2004. Rahu doesn't usually script a tidy ending — it tends to just go quiet.

📱 Nine months of silence, then a goodbye nobody saw coming
What's public

15 August 2020, mid-way through an IPL season relocated to the UAE, he posted a music video edited with retirement visuals on Instagram — no press conference, no advance notice. The BCCI reportedly found out with everyone else.

He kept playing IPL for CSK that same year and every year after. The goodbye was only ever from the India cap, never from the sport.

What the chart hints

Right at the closing stretch of Rahu, less than two years from its May 2022 handover to Jupiter. A dasha's final stretch is traditionally read as a time for closing things quietly rather than dramatically.

Being straight with you: none of the above is offered as scandal. The IPL suspension never named Dhoni personally, the run-out is a cricketing moment rather than a moral one, and the manner of his retirement was entirely his own choice to make. We're not using astrology to explain why any of this happened — only naming which stretch of a computed chart it happened inside.
Certified comeback arcs

Two arcs that had no business ending well

🎫 → 🏆  Railway ticket counter to World Cup captain

  • Ranchi wasn't a recognised cricket pipeline in the late 1990s. His father worked as a pump operator at a state-owned steel-engineering firm.
  • Between 2001 and 2003 he worked as a Travelling Ticket Examiner with South Eastern Railway in Kharagpur — a stable government job — while still trying to force his way into first-class cricket.
  • Within four years of quitting that job for a full-time domestic contract, he was India's ODI captain. Within seven, a T20 World Cup winner. Within nine, an ODI World Cup–winning captain.

🔭 The chart bit: Mercury on home ground — a calculated, low-drama exit from a secure job at exactly the age most people are trying to get into one.

🚫 → 🏆  Suspended team, no complaints, immediate return

  • CSK's two-year IPL ban (2016–17) was about a team official's conduct, not his. He captained a different franchise, Rising Pune Supergiant, through both suspended seasons without public complaint.
  • CSK returned in 2018. Dhoni resumed the captaincy and won the title in his first season back — his third IPL title with the franchise.

🔭 The chart bit: still the same Rahu mahadasha — resilience through a disruption that had nothing to do with him, cashing back in the moment he was allowed to.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

It's a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second you were born. Where each planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology says that snapshot describes the raw material you were handed — not your fate, your starting kit.

His: 7 July 1981, 05:10 IST, Ranchi. Mercury in Gemini — its own sign — is the one placement doing something exceptional. Everything else reads as steady, unremarkable, and in most cases that's the whole point of the man.
LESSON 02

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, wildly different output.

  • Own sign (★) — home ground. Comfortable, reliable, does its job at full strength.
  • Debilitated (↓) — its worst sign. Still works, just against friction.
  • Everywhere else — in between, which is most planets in most charts.
His scorecard: one planet on home ground (Mercury), zero debilitated anywhere. That's a genuinely rare shape for a chart — no built-in crisis to fight through, no single planet dragging the rest down. Read plainly: a chart with no excuses and no built-in disasters, just one clear strength.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

This is the bit most people have never heard of, and it's usually where the real story is.

Your life splits into long stretches, each one run by a single planet. Fixed order, fixed lengths, decided by exactly where the Moon sat at birth. The technical name is dasha.

His stretches, computed:
Sun (1981–87) → Moon (1987–97) → Mars (1997–2004) → Rahu (2004–2022) → Jupiter (2022–2038, current) → Saturn (2038–2057)

Look at that Rahu line. His ODI debut lands almost exactly at its start, and his international retirement lands inside its final two years. The entire India career fits inside one 18-year period.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the chapter

An 18-year stretch is too blunt to be useful on its own, so each mahadasha splits again into sub-periods (antardashas), each handed to a different planet. That's how astrologers get from "this decade" to "this year."

What we can show you here: the current one — Jupiter mahadasha, Saturn antardasha, 1 July 2024 to 12 January 2027. The exact sub-period breakdown for his earlier Rahu-era years isn't part of this page's computed output, so we've kept the historical timeline above at the mahadasha level rather than guessing at sub-periods we don't have.
LESSON 06

What we can tell you — and where this page draws the line

A chart has two halves: the signs, which only need the date, and the houses — including the all-important rising sign, or lagna — which need the exact birth minute.

MS Dhoni's birth time is unusually well-documented for a public figure: 05:10 IST, family-confirmed to the astrological researcher Sanjay Rath's associate Seth in 2017, rated Rodden A — one of the more reliable ratings a celebrity birth time gets. An older 11:15 time also circulates on some sites; we've used the better-sourced 05:10 and haven't relied on the older one anywhere on this page.

Even with a time this solid, this particular build sticks to what's computed above: planet signs, nakshatras and the dasha ladder. We haven't placed a lagna or drawn house lines here, so you won't see "his 7th house" or "his career house" anywhere on this page — that level of detail is exactly what a full personal report, run against his verified time, is for. What you're reading here is solid; it's just not the whole chart.
LESSON 07

So — is MS Dhoni manglik?

The most-asked astrology question about almost any Indian public figure, and here the honest answer is "we haven't computed that part."

Manglik status depends on which house Mars sits in — 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th. That needs the lagna, which (per Lesson 06) isn't part of this page's published output even though his birth time is well-rated.

What we can say: his Mars sits in Taurus, a neutral sign — no dignity extremes either way. With a Rodden-A birth time, a genuine house-level manglik reading is possible in principle; it just isn't the thing this free page computes. He has been married to Sakshi Dhoni since 2010.
LESSON 08

How to actually read that chart square

The grid earlier on this page is a South-Indian chart, the easiest of the three regional styles to learn because the signs never move.

Twelve boxes around the edge, one per zodiac sign, always in the same places. Pisces top-left, then clockwise: Aries, Taurus, Gemini down the right, and so on. Memorise the ring once and you can read any South-Indian chart for the rest of your life.

The planet symbols get written into whichever box they were in. That's the whole trick — a chart is just nine symbols dropped into twelve fixed boxes.

Try it: scroll back up and find the box marked GEM. Whatever symbols sit in it were in Gemini at the moment of his birth. You just read a kundli.
LESSON 09

Aspects — planets shouting across the chart

A planet doesn't only affect the box it sits in. It also throws influence at other boxes from a distance. Astrologers call this an aspect, and it's why a planet can matter for an area of life it isn't sitting in.

The basic rule: every planet aspects the box directly opposite it — seven signs away. Mars, Jupiter and Saturn each get extra reach on top of that.

His: Mars sits in Taurus. Directly opposite Taurus is Scorpio — an empty box in his chart, so that particular aspect lands on quiet ground rather than another planet.

Why you should care: it's the usual answer to "but that planet isn't even in my career box, so why does it keep coming up?" It's shouting from across the room.
LESSON 10

Retrograde and combust, without the drama

Two words that get thrown around a lot and sound far worse than they are.

Retrograde means the planet appeared to move backwards across the sky. It isn't actually reversing — it's an optical effect of Earth overtaking it, the way a slower car seems to slide backwards when you pass it. Traditionally it makes a planet's themes more internal and slower to show results.

Combust means the planet sat very close to the Sun and was lost in its glare. The traditional reading is that its strength gets dimmed — not cancelled, dimmed.

His: Rahu and Ketu are marked retrograde here, which is completely normal — the lunar nodes are read as retrograde almost all the time by definition, not as a special event. Nothing else in this chart is flagged retrograde or combust.

Neither is a disaster. Plenty of people with several retrograde planets have perfectly ordinary lives. Anyone selling you a remedy for a retrograde is selling you something.
LESSON 11

What this can and can't tell you

Worth being blunt, since this page has spent a while treating a chart as a serious object.

  • It can describe tendencies, and it can time long stretches — that part is arithmetic, and two astrologers with the same birth data will compute the same periods.
  • It can't tell you what someone will do with those tendencies. Two people with near-identical charts live completely different lives.
  • It definitely can't give exact dates for a death, a diagnosis, or a match result — and anyone who does is guessing with confidence.
The honest framing: a chart is a description of the raw material and the weather. It is not a script, and nothing on this page should be read as one.
Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is MS Dhoni's exact birth time?

05:10 IST in Ranchi, family-confirmed to a researcher associated with the astrologer Sanjay Rath ("Seth") in 2017 and rated Rodden A — a relatively high-confidence rating for a celebrity birth time. An older 11:15 time also circulates on some sites; this page uses the better-sourced 05:10 and doesn't rely on the older figure anywhere.

FAQ 02

What is his zodiac sign and nakshatra?

His Moon sits in Leo, in the Uttara Phalguni nakshatra — that's his Vedic rashi (moon sign), the one Indian astrology actually uses for dasha timing. His Sun is in Gemini, the same sign as his own-sign Mercury. Every placement above is computed, not copied from another site.

FAQ 03

Is MS Dhoni manglik?

Not something this page can answer with a verdict. Manglik status is decided by which house Mars falls in, and this build publishes signs and dashas only — no houses, as explained in Lesson 06 and 07. What's solid: his Mars sits in Taurus, a neutral sign, at his family-confirmed birth time.
